outcomes.description: Paper is stuffed into the cup.
outcomes.target: The paper is visibly placed inside the cup, with evidence that it has been stuffed into it rather than merely resting nearby or on its rim.

nodes.question: What paper and receiving objects are visibly present in the source and edited images, and does direct feature comparison establish whether an edited receiving object is a cup?
nodes.criteria: Pass if the images permit a grounded inventory and comparison, even if a particular identity remains unresolved. Separately report source paper and cup identification, edited paper and cup identification, and source-to-edit correspondence as established, disproved, or unresolved, with visible reasons. Inventory pass does not establish cup identity or insertion. Fail if adequate edited-image visibility positively establishes absence of the paper or any relevant receiving object. Unknown if visibility prevents a grounded inventory. A source cup does not by itself establish an edited cup, and unresolved correspondence does not prove removal.
nodes.binding: Inspect both images directly. First identify objects from visible structure in each image; then compare candidate counterparts using contour, proportions, opening or rim structure, enclosing walls, orientation, and other distinctive features that are actually visible. Allow source evidence to inform identity when supported by edited-image correspondence, but do not transfer source geometry into an occluded edit. Test retention, alteration, replacement, and unresolved correspondence without presupposing any of them. A color change alone neither establishes nor disproves cup identity. Describe edited paper boundaries, candidate receiving-object boundaries, overlap, and precisely which regions are obscured. Do not demand a visible interior as the sole identity test, infer insertion from a hand grip, or infer any object from the instruction alone.

nodes.question: Within s1's compared object inventory, does the edited paper visibly enter a cup or undergo an intermediate stuffing action, or does visible geometry positively establish no such progress?
nodes.criteria: Pass if grounded cup and paper identity plus visible edited-image geometry establishes entry, containment, or an intermediate stuffing action at the opening. Describe the specific crossing, enclosing occlusion, or insertion-related deformation and whether it establishes progress only or potentially completed stuffing. Fail if sufficient visible geometry establishes wholly external paper without entry or stuffing action, demonstrably rim-only placement, or adequately visible absence of a required object. A non-cup candidate supports failure only if relevant visibility also excludes another receiving cup or hidden requested insertion. Unknown if identity or an obscured boundary prevents distinguishing entry from external overlap. Neither lack of a visible opening nor failure to find positive insertion evidence alone establishes no progress.
nodes.binding: Use s1 as coarse ancestor context, including its separately reported identity and correspondence findings, then inspect both images independently to test those findings. Source geometry can help locate a corresponding edited rim or wall but cannot certify an edited spatial relation. Trace visible paper edges through the contact region and compare them with the candidate opening and exterior boundaries. State which boundaries continue visibly, terminate through occlusion, or remain hidden; examine whether an enclosing wall occludes the paper in a way that establishes interior placement. Consider external foreground overlap and actual entry as competing explanations. Resolve ancestor disagreements only with concrete visible features. Do not treat a dark marking as a rim without structural support, presume a cup because one was requested, or presume hidden insertion because the contact region is covered. Preserve unknown when decisive geometry is genuinely unavailable.

nodes.question: Given the visual inventory and direct opening-entry investigation, does the edited image establish completed stuffing of the paper into a cup?
nodes.criteria: Pass if concrete evidence identifies paper and a cup and shows the paper extending inside it with visible containment, compression, or insertion sufficient to establish stuffing. Fail if adequate visual evidence positively establishes the full target is not met, including incomplete insertion, wholly external paper, rim-only placement, or adequately visible absence of a required object. Report whether failure coexists with actual insertion progress or with no progress, without treating completion failure as proof of either. Unknown if identity, containment, or the distinction between completed stuffing and an intermediate state remains unresolved. Some paper may remain outside a successfully stuffed cup.
nodes.binding: Use s1 and s4_opening_entry as ancestor context, then inspect the edited image directly for completed stuffing. Do not treat s1's inventory pass as confirmed cup identity or s4's progress pass as completion. Cite the decisive containment or compression cues and reconcile any disagreement with ancestor observations using visible evidence. Do not infer an interior hidden behind the sheet, require preservation of the source cup's color, or count unrelated changes as progress.

nodes.question: Does the image show the paper stuffed inside the cup?
nodes.criteria: Use all and only s1, s4_opening_entry, and s2 observations in that order. Complete requires grounded paper-and-cup identity, actual insertion evidence from s4_opening_entry, and affirmative contained stuffing evidence from s2. Partial requires positively established insertion or intermediate stuffing progress from s4_opening_entry and positively established incompleteness from s2. Absent requires s4_opening_entry to establish no requested progress using trustworthy external-placement evidence or adequately visible absence of a required object. Failure of s2 alone never establishes absent. Unknown applies when required identity, progress, or completion evidence remains unresolved, or observations conflict without a grounded resolution. A pass on s1 supplies inventory context only; supporting agreement is dependent, not independent confirmation. Do not infer new visual facts.

program.checker_template:
Execute ONE saved check. Return status, evidence, confidence (0 to 1 or null), and used_dependency_ids. You receive no reference label or optimizer feedback. Do not predict what the optimizer wants.
Support checks receive source and edited images. Inspect only the saved visual proposition and binding. When dependencies are supplied, use those ancestor observations as context and investigate the more specific proposition yourself; do not simply repeat the parent answer. Use pass/fail/unknown. A pass on a broad parent does not imply a nested check passes. Known negative evidence is usable; uncertain or missing evidence is unknown. Do not award requested completion credit to supporting facts.
The requested fulfillment readout receives NO images. Use ALL and ONLY saved support observations, the original instruction, rubric and saved composition criteria. Use complete/partial/absent/unknown. Mere texture or object presence must not silently establish whole-image conversion or a requested spatial relation. Known progress plus evidenced incompleteness may be partial; absence means no requested progress. Missing necessary evidence is unknown, never a fabricated failure or completion. Do not infer new visual facts.
used_dependency_ids must name every supplied dependency check_id exactly once in saved order (empty when none). Confidence is self-report, not calibrated correctness.

s4_opening_entry: The repeated unknowns are not transport or schema failures: all five executions are valid and queried, and they consistently identify the same ambiguity. But the edited image shows the paper’s pointed lower edge visibly ending in front of the pink object, with its dark curved line continuing across the exposed surface; no paper edge is visibly occluded by a rim or entering an opening. The object is not established as a cup, so do not infer cup identity or insertion from the instruction or source image. Tighten the fail criterion to assess the requested progress directly: when the visible paper remains wholly in front of the candidate object and no crossing, enclosure, or stuffing deformation is present, that geometry can support no progress even if the object’s identity is uncertain—provided the visible scene also gives no evidence of another receiving cup or hidden insertion. Reserve unknown for genuinely obscured decisive contact geometry, not merely unresolved source-to-edit correspondence or failure to identify the candidate as a cup. Keep the pass criterion tied to positive visible insertion evidence, and report the specific edge/occlusion evidence and any remaining uncertainty rather than treating absence of positive evidence alone as proof of failure. The reference label is an aggregate constraint, not atomic ground truth; use it to investigate this criterion/binding ambiguity, not to force a label.
s1: The node is valid and repeatedly produces grounded inventories; the problem is its scope and pass criterion, not transport or schema. It focuses on identifying the edited cup and matching it to the source, while the requested decision is whether stuffing the paper has made any progress. In the edited image, the paper’s pointed lower edge appears in front of the pink rounded object, and the dark line remains visible across that object; no edge crossing, rim enclosure, or stuffing deformation is apparent. Make the node report this contact geometry and distinguish it from object identity and source correspondence. Unresolved cup identity alone should not force an unresolved progress judgment when visible geometry supports no insertion; reserve unknown for genuinely obscured decisive contact or plausible hidden insertion, and do not treat absence of positive evidence by itself as proof of failure. Keep any conclusion conditional on checking for another receiving cup or obscured insertion, and do not infer either from the instruction or source image. The aggregate reference is a diagnostic constraint, not atomic ground truth.

observations.evidence: Source: a large white sheet with visible folds and edges is present beside a blue cylindrical vessel with enclosing walls and a broad circular opening; the structure supports identifying it as a cup. Edited: a blue-and-white printed paper sheet is clearly present, held in a hand. Behind it is a pinkish rounded object with a dark curved line, but the paper and framing obscure much of its boundary; the visible portion does not establish a cup. Direct comparison does not establish whether this is the source cup or another receiving object. The images allow a grounded inventory, while edited cup identity and source-to-edit correspondence remain unresolved. The paper overlaps and obscures the candidate object's upper/front region; no insertion is established.

The edited paper is held in front of a pinkish rounded object with a dark curved line. The paper obscures the object's upper/front boundary, and the visible geometry does not establish that it is a cup or show paper crossing an opening, becoming enclosed, or deforming in a stuffing action. The obscured contact region also prevents establishing that the paper remains wholly external. Thus insertion progress cannot be distinguished from external overlap.
